subject: Follow-up: price corridor & packaging amortization — proposed redlines
messages:
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Park <john.park@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing exhibit question — corridor, amortization and early true-up

Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. The pricing exhibit you shared looks close but procurement has two outstanding items we need clarified before we route to legal:

1) Discount corridor construction: the exhibit defines a corridor that floors our unit price for months 1–6 and then re-evaluates. Procurement is concerned the corridor math may effectively double-dip with the monthly true-up. Can you confirm whether the corridor is applied before or after any monthly true-up adjustments? A short worked example would be helpful.

2) Packaging amortization: our accounting prefers a 12-month amortization of any upfront packaging credits rather than treating them as immediate rebate. The order form currently has a 24-month amortization. What flexibility do you have here?

3) Early termination true-up: the redline we received earlier included an early true-up clause tied to realized usage. We need a simple cap so that, in the event of a termination in year 1, our liability is limited (propose 6 months of the amortized amount).

Can you get us a marked-up exhibit and a short note explaining the math? If possible we want to close this week.

Best,
Dana

--
Dana Liu
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Health
+dana.liu@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: John Park <john.park@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Sep 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit question — corridor, amortization and early true-up

Dana —

Thanks for the clear list. Appreciate the target of closing this week; we should be able to meet that. I’m looping in Karthik (pricing/legal lead) and Laura (billing ops) to provide a marked-up exhibit and the worked examples.

Attached: pricing-exhibit-amortization-redline.docx (redline with comments) and a short spreadsheet that shows:
- Corridor application order (we apply corridor floor before monthly true-ups by default)
- Two worked scenarios (lower usage than committed, and over-usage with monthly true-up applied)

High level answers:
- Corridor vs true-up: corridor sets a floor on per-unit billable price at the invoice line-item level. Monthly true-up reconciles committed vs actual usage; if true-up increases net payable, the corridor floor precludes per-unit price dropping below the floor while amortized credits reduce the net balance. The example in the attached spreadsheet illustrates month-by-month cash flows.
- Amortization: we can move to 12-month amortization for the upfront packaging credit on this deal if ACME prefers; that will increase monthly cash outflow compared to 24 months, so we note it may affect monthly invoice amounts and any early termination math.
- Early termination cap: we are open to a 6-month cap on the unamortized packaging credit in year 1; Karthik has massaged language that preserves our right to true-up usage while capping the customer liability.

Karthik / Laura — please see Dana’s note below. Karthik, I left a couple inline suggestions in the redline but can you draft a clean clause for the early termination cap (6 months) and confirm the corridor-first interpretation? Laura, can you confirm the billing implications if we switch to 12-month amortization (collections cadence, invoice line items)?

Dana — I’ll follow up once Karthik and Laura have final wording. Attached redline is the first pass.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, East
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acmehealth.com>, John Park <john.park@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Sep 2028 13:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit question — corridor, amortization and early true-up

Marissa / Laura / Dana —

I reviewed Marissa’s redline and attached a suggested clean clause (see pricing-exhibit-amortization-redline.docx). Key points and rationale below. I included inline comments in the docx for the billing and legal teams.

Summary:
- Corridor application: confirm corridor floor is applied at the per-unit line item before monthly true-ups. Practical effect: customers never see a per-unit invoice below the stated floor; true-ups reconcile total spend against commitment and will use the corridor-adjusted per-unit amounts when calculating any additional charges or refunds.
- Amortization: Redwood will accept a 12-month amortization of packaging credits for the ACME deal. Billing needs to show (a) amortization schedule as a separate invoice line labeled "Pack Credit Amortization" and (b) remaining unamortized balance on each invoice.
- Early termination cap: proposed clean clause language below (redline attached). It limits customer liability on unamortized packaging credits to six (6) months of the then-current amortization amount if termination occurs within the first 12 months. That preserves our right to true-up usage for committed volumes while limiting the absolute amount owed on the upfront credit.

Proposed clause (for insertion into Exhibit B — Pricing):
"In the event of termination by Customer within the first twelve (12) months following the Effective Date, Customer’s sole liability with respect to any unamortized packaging credit shall not exceed the equivalent of six (6) months of the then-current monthly amortization amount. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood retains the right to true-up Customer usage against committed volumes in accordance with Section 3 of the Order Form; any true-up amount shall be calculated using per-unit invoice prices after application of the corridor floor."

Laura: operational asks — please confirm the exact invoice line label and whether accounting can include the remaining unamortized balance on month-end statements. Also confirm whether the finance team requires a distinct AR code for amortized credits.

Dana / John: if that language looks acceptable, we can produce a clean PDF and DocuSign-ready orderform today. If ACME wants the cap tied to a dollar amount instead of months, suggest we discuss numbers; otherwise six-months is our standard concession for packaging on early-termination in pilot-sized deals.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Pricing & Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
